title: Banner form has no placement control — every admin-created banner is placement:'app', so the web storefront hero can never be filled
detail: `placementRef` is a `useRef<BannerPlacement>(seed?.placement ?? 'app')` (line 41), set only from the loaded doc (line 66) and passed straight to `saveBanner` (line 129). There is no `<Select>`, toggle or any other UI anywhere in the form (or the list) that lets an admin change it, and no filter/column that even shows it. `BANNER_PLACEMENTS = ['app','website']` (packages/shared/src/enums.ts:207). The web storefront reads ONLY the other value: web/src/lib/banners.ts:23 `query(collection(db,'banners'), where('placement','==',BANNER_PLACEMENTS[1]))` i.e. 'website'; the app reads `where('placement', isEqualTo: 'app')` (app/lib/features/catalog/data/catalog_repository.dart:100). So 100% of banners created through the admin land in the app bucket, and the web hero (`HeroBanner`, rendered only when `banners.length > 0`, web/src/app/(shop)/page.tsx:48) can never be populated after the seed docs are gone.
failure_scenario: Marketing opens Growth ▸ Banner ▸ + Add banner, uploads the Eid hero artwork, titles it "The Eid Edit", turns on Publish live and saves. It appears in the app carousel but never on the website — the storefront keeps showing the hardcoded "Royal Oud, reimagined" fallback hero. There is no control in the admin to move it, and nothing in the UI explains why.
fix: Add a required placement Select (options from `BANNER_PLACEMENTS`) to the form, default it explicitly on create, show the placement on the list cards, and let the list filter by it. Replace `placementRef` with real form state so the value round-trips on edit.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. In BannerFormPage.tsx placement lives solely in `placementRef` (line 41, default 'app'), is reassigned only from the loaded doc (line 66) and consumed only at save (line 129) — no Select/Toggle/radio/tab anywhere in the form, and BannerListPage.tsx (read in full) has no placement column, badge, filter or tab either, so the field is neither settable nor visible in the admin. saveBanner (admin/src/features/banner/api/banners.ts) writes `placement: values.placement` verbatim with no server-side default, and a grep for `banners` across admin/src, functions/src and firebase/ shows the admin client is the ONLY writer of the collection — no Cloud Function, no rules default, no other surface can correct it. Consumers are exactly as claimed: web/src/lib/banners.ts:23 queries placement=='website' (BANNER_PLACEMENTS[1]) and app catalog_repository.dart:100 queries placement=='app', with web/src/app/(shop)/page.tsx:48 rendering HeroBanner only when banners.length>0. Therefore every admin-created banner is 'app' and the web hero can never be filled. The ALREADY-FIXED list only covers the web-side enum drift ('web'→'website'), which fixes the read query but not the missing write control; not on the KNOWN-INTENTIONAL list. The only accidental workaround is editing the seeded banners/banner_2 (placement preserved via line 66), and even that seed doc has imageUrl:'' so it is filtered out — in a production DB there is no 'website' banner and no way to create one.

title: Flash sale campaigns (flashSales) have no admin screen at all, yet an active seeded sale silently overrides the per-product Flash sale toggle on the web home page
detail: The GROWTH nav group has no Flash Sale entry and `router.tsx` has no `/flash-sale` route (it is not in `ALL_NAV_ITEMS`, so it doesn't even get a `ModulePlaceholder`). Nothing under admin/src writes the `flashSales` collection — a grep for `flashSales` across admin/functions/web/app returns only scripts/seed.ts:771 and the readers. But the collection is fully wired everywhere else: firestore.rules:58 allows `canWrite('flashSale')`, firestore.indexes.json:100 has an index for it, `FlashSale`/`FlashSaleOverride` exist in packages/shared/src/types/commerce.ts:45-63, and web/src/lib/flashSale.ts:16 subscribes to `where('status','==','active')`. Worse, `flashSaleProducts()` (web/src/lib/flashSale.ts:35) returns `sale.productIds` and IGNORES the `isFlashSale` product flags whenever a sale doc is active, and the home page countdown pill is driven by `sale.endsAt` (page.tsx:39). The functions comment at functions/src/index.ts:76 promises a `flashSaleStatusFlip` sweep that does not exist in functions/src/scheduled/sweeps.ts (only `couponExpirySweep` is exported), so nothing can flip the status either.
failure_scenario: An admin turns on "Flash sale" for 5 perfumes in Products ▸ Edit (ProductFormPage.tsx:389). The web home flash-sale rail keeps showing products '1','2','7' from `flashSales/flash_1` and a countdown to a date nobody can see or change, because the seeded sale is still `status:'active'`. The admin has no screen to open, edit, end or delete that sale, and no explanation for why their toggles do nothing.
fix: Either build the Flash Sale module (list/create/edit of `flashSales`: name, window, status, productIds, overrides, visibility) plus a nav entry and route, or delete the collection from rules/indexes/shared types and make web/src/lib/flashSale.ts derive the rail purely from `isFlashSale` + a settings-driven countdown.

verdict.reason:
Could not refute — every checkable element of the claim holds, and nothing on the ALREADY-FIXED / KNOWN-INTENTIONAL lists covers it.

Confirmed by inspection:
- /home/h/barkath/admin/src/components/layout/navConfig.tsx GROWTH group = Spinner, Coupons, Affiliate, Banner, Notifications only. No Flash Sale item, so it is absent from ALL_NAV_ITEMS (line 85).
- /home/h/barkath/admin/src/app/router.tsx has no /flash-sale route; its placeholder catch-all is derived from ALL_NAV_ITEMS (`ALL_NAV_ITEMS.filter((i) => !BUILT.has(i.path))`), so the module gets not even a ModulePlaceholder — the path is simply unroutable.
- `grep -rn "flashSale" /home/h/barkath/admin/src` returns ONLY the product-level flag/filter (ProductFormPage.tsx:391 toggle, ProductsFilterPage, products/api) and the sub-admin permission label at /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/subadmin/api/subadmin.ts:50 (`flashSale: 'Flash Sale'`). Nothing anywhere in admin/, functions/, web/, or app/ WRITES the `flashSales` collection — only /home/h/barkath/scripts/seed.ts:771 does.
- The collection is otherwise fully wired: /home/h/barkath/firebase/firestore.rules:58 `match /flashSales/{id} { ... allow write: if canWrite('flashSale'); }`; /home/h/barkath/firebase/firestore.indexes.json:126 index on status+endsAt; `flashSale` is a real ModuleKey (/home/h/barkath/packages/shared/src/enums.ts:267) so a sub-admin can be granted create/edit/delete on a screen that does not exist; `FlashSale`/`FlashSaleOverride` types at /home/h/barkath/packages/shared/src/types/commerce.ts:45-63; `flashSales` in collections.ts:15.
- Web really does let the campaign win over the toggles: /home/h/barkath/web/src/lib/flashSale.ts:35 `if (!sale || sale.productIds.length === 0) return fallback;` — when a sale is active it returns `sale.productIds` and the `isFlashSale`-flagged list is only the fallback. The home page comment at web/src/app/(shop)/page.tsx:34-36 states this is deliberate ("An admin flash-sale campaign, when live, still takes precedence"), which makes the missing admin CRUD worse, not better: the surface intentionally defers to a doc no admin can create, edit, or end. The countdown pill is driven by `sale.endsAt` (page.tsx:40), and the rail's empty label still tells admins to "turn on 'Flash sale' for a product in the admin" — advice that is wrong while a sale is active.
- The functions comment at /home/h/barkath/functions/src/index.ts:76 does promise `flashSaleStatusFlip`; /home/h/barkath/functions/src/scheduled/sweeps.ts exports only `sweepExpiredCoupons` and `couponExpirySweep`. No such sweep exists.
- Consistency bonus: the Flutter app ignores `flashSales` entirely (app/lib/features/catalog/data/catalog_repository.dart:187 `where((p) => p.isFlashSale)`), so app and web disagree about what the flash rail means, and only web is affected by the unmanageable campaign doc.

Two fair caveats that reduce blast radius but not validity: (a) the seeded sale window is daysAgo(1)→daysAhead(1) and useActiveFlashSale checks the window client-side, so the override self-heals ~24h after seeding even without a status flip — the "countdown to a date nobody can change" is time-bounded rather than permanent; (b) in a fresh production project with no sale doc the per-product toggles work fine, so the visible symptom needs a sale doc to exist. Neither refutes the defect: the `flashSale` module is granted in permissions and rules, indexed, typed, and consumed by web, yet has zero write path in the admin — an admin can neither create a campaign (the intended feature) nor end/delete one that exists. That is a genuine, fixable broken-CRUD gap, distinct from `newArrivals`, whose module key is also screenless but whose web rail is explicitly automatic ("no admin flag", page.tsx:24).

title: Banner edit swallows a failed load: getBanner has no catch, leaving a permanent spinner and an unhandled rejection
detail: `getBanner(routeId!).then((b) => { ... setLoading(false); })` (lines 60-74) has no `.catch()`. `loading` is initialised to `!isNew && !seed` (line 39), and the component early-returns a full-page `<Spinner>` while loading (lines 137-143). If the read rejects — permission-denied for a sub-admin without banner view, offline, or a rules deploy blip — `setLoading(false)` never runs, no toast fires, and the promise rejection is unhandled. There is no error branch at all in this component (unlike BannerListPage, which does render an error card).
failure_scenario: An admin opens a banner edit link directly (page refresh or a shared URL, so the `getCachedList` seed at line 36 is empty) while offline or with a stale token. The screen shows a spinner forever with no message and no way back other than the browser back button; the console logs an unhandled promise rejection.
fix: Add `.catch(() => { toast.error('Couldn’t load this banner.'); navigate('/banner'); })` (or set an error state and render a retry card), and always clear `loading` in a `finally`.

verdict.reason: The core code claim is accurate and I could not refute it. In /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/banner/routes/BannerFormPage.tsx:60-74 the getBanner promise has no .catch(), and `loading` (line 39) is cleared only inside the success callback (line 73), while lines 144-150 early-return a bare full-page Spinner. getBanner is a plain getDoc (/home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/banner/api/banners.ts:39), which rejects with `unavailable` when the client is offline and the doc is not in the local cache — reachable on a direct link or refresh, since the getCachedList seed (line 35) is empty then. There is no mitigation anywhere: the admin app has no ErrorBoundary, no router errorElement (/home/h/barkath/admin/src/app/router.tsx), and no unhandledrejection handler. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists. Two sub-claims ARE wrong, which lowers severity: (1) the "sub-admin permission-denied" trigger is impossible — /home/h/barkath/firebase/firestore.rules:69 allows banner reads to everyone (`allow read: if hasAppCheck()`, and hasAppCheck() is hard-coded `return true` at line 49); only writes are role-gated. (2) "no way back other than browser back" is false — the page renders inside AppShell, so the sidebar/top bar remain clickable. Also note this is a systemic pattern, not banner-specific: the same uncaught .then() with success-only setLoading(false) appears in ProductFormPage.tsx:109-133, CategoryFormPage.tsx:54-70 and CouponFormPage.tsx:90. Net: a real, one-line-fixable stuck-state defect, but low severity with a network/offline-only trigger.

title: Broadcast is recorded as fully 'sent' with full reach BEFORE the fan-out runs, and the fan-out is unbounded
detail: broadcast.ts:43-48 writes the `broadcasts` doc with `reach: customers.size, opened: 0, status: 'sent'` first, and only then (lines 51-62) loops `for (i += 450)` committing per-user inbox batches. `targetCustomers('all')` is a bare `col.get()` of the ENTIRE customers collection with no limit or pagination (line 26), and callableOpts (functions/src/_lib/admin.ts:25-33) sets no timeoutSeconds, so the callable dies at the v2 default of 60s. If any batch commit throws or the function times out, the CF rejects — but the broadcasts doc is already persisted claiming status 'sent' and the full reach. Nothing ever rewrites it to 'failed'. There is also no idempotency key, so a retry re-fans-out from customer #0.
failure_scenario: Admin sends to "All users" with 30k customers. The function commits ~12k inbox rows, then hits the 60s timeout. The admin sees the toast "Couldn't send the notification…" from cfError, but navigating to /notifications shows a row: Status=Sent, Sent=30,000, Opened=0. Believing it failed, the admin clicks Send again — the first 12k customers now get the identical notification twice, and a second bogus "Sent 30,000" row appears in the log.
fix: Write the broadcast doc with status 'sending' first, fan out, then update to 'sent' (or 'failed' + the partial reach) in a finally/catch. Raise timeoutSeconds and page `customers` with a cursor (or move the fan-out to a task queue / Firestore-triggered worker) so a 30k-customer audience cannot exceed the callable budget.

verdict.reason: Claim verified against source. functions/src/notifications/broadcast.ts:43-48 persists the broadcasts doc with status:'sent', reach: customers.size and opened: 0 BEFORE the per-user inbox fan-out at lines 51-62, and targetCustomers('all') at line 26 is a bare col.get() of the whole customers collection with no limit/cursor. callableOpts in functions/src/_lib/admin.ts:25-33 sets no timeoutSeconds and a repo-wide grep for timeoutSeconds/maxInstances in functions/src returns nothing, so the callable runs at the v2 60s default. Nothing ever repairs the record: grepping 'broadcasts' across functions/src, packages/shared/src, firebase/ and scripts/ yields only firebase/firestore.rules:264 (CF-only write) — there is no reconciler, no 'sending' state, and no code path anywhere writes status:'failed' for a broadcast, even though admin/src/features/notifications/api/notifications.ts:17 and broadcastBadge declare and render both. There is no idempotency key: the zod schema accepts only title/body/audience/deepLink, and a retry mints a fresh doc ref and restarts the loop at i=0. The UX half also checks out: NotificationCreatePage.tsx:101-102 toasts cfError on rejection while NotificationsListPage.tsx:88-104 renders the persisted 'Sent' badge and full reach, and the row menu offers 'Send similar', so a duplicate fan-out is the natural admin response. Any single batch.commit() rejection triggers the same permanent lie, so the defect does not depend on the report's specific 30k/60s scale arithmetic (the one unverifiable part). Not on the already-fixed list (that entry covers markBroadcastOpened/opened counting and the earlier FCM truncation fix, both distinct) and not on the known-intentional list. Real, reachable, fixable: write status:'sending' first, paginate the fan-out, update to 'sent' with the actual count, mark 'failed' on error, and accept an idempotency id.

title: Audience targeting ignores isBlocked and the customer's own notification opt-out preferences
detail: estimateReach (notifications.ts:91-106) filters only on `affiliate.enabled` / `createdAt`, and the server-side targetCustomers (functions/src/notifications/broadcast.ts:19-27) does exactly the same — neither excludes `isBlocked == true` (shared/src/types/customers.ts:119) nor honours `preferences.notificationsEnabled` / `preferences.notifyPromotions` (customers.ts:130-135). Those preference booleans ARE writable by the customer: web/src/app/(shop)/account/settings/notifications/page.tsx:46-52 does `updateDoc(customers/{uid}, {preferences: {...prefs, [key]: next}})` with a master "Push notifications" switch and a "Promotions & offers" switch. Grepping all four surfaces for `notificationsEnabled|notifyPromotions` returns only that writer, the app's account-creation defaults (app/lib/features/auth/data/auth_repository.dart:251) and seed.ts:462 — no reader anywhere. So the web opt-out toggles are dead controls and every broadcast lands in every inbox regardless.
failure_scenario: A customer opens Account → Settings → Notifications on web and turns OFF "Promotions & offers". The admin sends a promo broadcast to All users; the CF still writes customers/{uid}/notifications for that customer and the bell dot lights up — the toggle they flipped does nothing. Separately, after blocking 200 abusive accounts (whose Firebase Auth users are disabled by adminBlockUser), the create screen still reports "Estimated reach: 1,240 users" and the stored reach counts those 200 accounts that can never sign in, permanently deflating the Opened/Sent ratio.
fix: Filter both sides identically: in targetCustomers add `.where('isBlocked','==',false)` (or skip blocked docs in the fan-out loop) and skip customers whose `preferences.notificationsEnabled === false`, plus `notifyPromotions === false` for promo broadcasts; mirror the same two predicates in estimateReach so the admin's number matches what the CF will actually write.

verdict.reason: Verified and could not refute. estimateReach (admin/src/features/notifications/api/notifications.ts:91-106) filters only affiliate.enabled/createdAt and returns customers.length for 'all', fed by the unfiltered useCustomersList() at NotificationCreatePage.tsx:45 (the same source whose rows render a 'Blocked' badge). The server mirrors it: targetCustomers (functions/src/notifications/broadcast.ts:19-27) does col.get() for 'all' with no isBlocked or preference clause, and that set drives both reach: customers.size and the per-user customers/{uid}/notifications writes at line 55 — the same denominator markBroadcastOpened increments against. Repo-wide grep for notificationsEnabled|notifyPromotions|notifyOrderUpdates across ts/tsx/dart/rules yields only four sites: the shared type (packages/shared/src/types/customers.ts:130-136), seed defaults (scripts/seed.ts:462), the app's account-creation defaults (app/lib/features/auth/data/auth_repository.dart:250), and the web writer (web/src/app/(shop)/account/settings/notifications/page.tsx:15-25,46-52). No reader exists. I checked every plausible escape hatch: the app inbox (app/lib/features/notifications/) does not filter on preferences on read; the push path cannot be the enforcement point because fcmTokens is written by nothing (grep finds it only in packages/shared/src/collections.ts:27, firebase/firestore.rules:239, and the CF read at broadcast.ts:73), so there is no token-deregistration-on-toggle substitute; firestore.rules:159 explicitly allows the customer to write 'preferences', so the toggle really persists; and adminSendBroadcastNotification is the only writer of customers/{uid}/notifications anywhere in functions/src, so no other path applies the filter. Not on the ALREADY-FIXED list (which covers broadcasts.opened counting, not audience filtering) nor KNOWN-INTENTIONAL. Severity differs between the halves: the preferences half is a genuine dead user-facing control; the isBlocked half is metrics correctness (blocked accounts, Auth-disabled by functions/src/customers/moderation.ts:22, still receive inbox docs and inflate reach). Both are real and fixable in the same two functions.

title: Deep-link product picker offers draft / archived / hidden products, and the app opens them without a status check
detail: productOptions is built from useProductsList() (NotificationCreatePage.tsx:47-50), which is documented as "All products (every status)" — admin/src/features/products/api/products.ts:21-25 queries `collection(db,'products')` with no status or visibility filter. categoryOptions likewise comes from useCategories() with no `visibility` filter (categories.ts:25-28). Nothing validates the chosen target before send, and the CF's zod schema only checks that `target` is a string (broadcast.ts:16). On the receiving end the app deep-links straight to the doc: notifications_screen.dart:174 pushes `/product/$target`, and CatalogRepository.productById (catalog_repository.dart:114-117) is a raw `doc(id).snapshots()` with NO status filter — while products are world-readable (firestore.rules:50-51).
failure_scenario: Admin picks the unreleased "Oud Royale (draft)" from the Product dropdown — it looks identical to published products in the list — and sends to All users. Every customer who taps the notification lands on a full product page for an unpublished item, price and all, and can add it to the bag. The category equivalent is quieter but still broken: deep-linking a hidden category opens a page whose grid is empty, because productsInCategory filters `status=='published'` (catalog_repository.dart:129).
fix: Restrict the pickers to publishable targets — filter productOptions to `p.status === 'published' && p.visibility !== 'hidden'` and categoryOptions to visible categories — and re-check the target's status server-side in adminSendBroadcastNotification before recording the broadcast.

verdict.reason:
Every link in the chain checks out; I could not find a guard anywhere.

1. Admin picker is unfiltered. /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/notifications/routes/NotificationCreatePage.tsx:47-54 builds productOptions from `useProductsList()` and categoryOptions from `useCategories()`. /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/products/api/products.ts:22-26 is `query(collection(db,'products'), orderBy('createdAt','desc'))` — no status/visibility/deletedAt filter, and its own doc comment says "All products (every status)". /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/categories/api/categories.ts:25-29 is `orderBy('order','asc')` with no visibility filter. Both `Product.status`/`Product.visibility` and `Category.visibility` exist in packages/shared/src/types/catalog.ts, so the filterable fields are there and simply unused. The dropdown labels are bare `p.name`, so a draft is visually indistinguishable from a published product.

2. No client-side validation. `validate()` (NotificationCreatePage.tsx:72-84) only checks non-emptiness of the target; nothing inspects the picked doc's status.

3. No server-side re-check. /home/h/barkath/functions/src/notifications/broadcast.ts:16 — `deepLink: z.object({ type: z.string(), target: z.string().nullable().optional() })`. The handler (lines 33-95) never loads the product/category doc; it writes deepLink straight to broadcasts/{id} and to every customers/{uid}/notifications doc.

4. App opens it raw. /home/h/barkath/app/lib/features/notifications/notifications_screen.dart:_onTap pushes `${Routes.product}/$target` for type 'product' with no lookup. /home/h/barkath/app/lib/features/catalog/data/catalog_repository.dart:114-117 `productById` is `doc(id).snapshots()` with no filter, and /home/h/barkath/app/lib/features/catalog/product_details_screen.dart renders `_Content` for any non-null doc — grep for status/visibility/published in that file returns zero hits, so a draft renders fully with price and add-to-bag. firebase/firestore.rules `match /products/{id} { allow read: if hasAppCheck(); }` with `hasAppCheck()` hardcoded `true`, so the read succeeds for any signed-in/anon client.

5. The category half is also real: `productsInCategory` filters `status=='published'` and drops `visibility=='hidden'` (catalog_repository.dart:~123-141), so deep-linking a hidden category yields an empty grid.

Refutation attempts that failed: not on the ALREADY-FIXED or KNOWN-INTENTIONAL lists; no fallback/guard in the app, CF, or rules; the path is plainly reachable (one dropdown pick). The only mitigating find is that /home/h/barkath/admin/src/features/banner/routes/BannerFormPage.tsx:260 uses the same unfiltered `products.map(...)` picker — i.e. the same gap exists on banners too, which makes it a repeated pattern rather than a one-off, not a reason it is correct. The fix is squarely in the admin: restrict deep-link target options to `status === 'published'` (and non-hidden) products / visible categories, matching what the storefront will actually show.

title: Custom URL deep link accepts any string — no scheme or format validation on either side
detail: The Link URL input (NotificationCreatePage.tsx:214-222) is a plain text field; validate() only checks `!target.trim()` (lines 79-81). The CF schema is `target: z.string().nullable().optional()` (broadcast.ts:16) — any string passes. The app deliberately refuses anything that isn't http/https: notifications_screen.dart:188-194 does `Uri.tryParse(target)` and only launches when `uri.scheme == 'http' || 'https'`, otherwise the tap does nothing at all (no error, no fallback). The placeholder "https://…" is the only hint the admin gets.
failure_scenario: Admin types `www.barkath.com/eid-sale` (no scheme) or `barkath://spin` into Link URL and sends. Every validation passes, the broadcast is recorded Sent, and every customer who taps the notification card gets absolutely nothing — the card stays inert with no error, and the admin has no way to tell from the Opened column that the destination was malformed.
fix: Validate in the create form (and mirror it in the zod schema): require the URL to parse and its protocol to be http: or https:, e.g. reject in validate() with 'Enter a full https:// URL'; optionally offer an in-app-route picker instead of free text for internal destinations.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on all three surfaces. Admin (NotificationCreatePage.tsx:214-222) renders the Link URL as a plain <input> with no type="url"/pattern and outside any <form>; validate() (lines 72-84) only rejects an empty target, so `www.barkath.com/sale` or `barkath://spin` passes. The CF schema (functions/src/notifications/broadcast.ts:16) is `target: z.string().nullable().optional()` with no refine and no normalization — it persists the string verbatim to broadcasts/{id} and to every customers/{uid}/notifications doc and marks status 'sent'. The app (app/lib/features/notifications/notifications_screen.dart:169-196) launches only when Uri.tryParse yields scheme http/https, and its own comment states this restriction is a deliberate security guard, so it will not be loosened; a scheme-less or custom-scheme target makes the card silently inert (no error, no fallback to home). Grep over web/, app/, functions/, packages/shared and admin/ shows the Flutter screen is the sole consumer of this deepLink object (the shared `deepLink: string` fields are the unrelated admin NotificationBell shape). The 'url' option is live in DEEP_LINK_TYPES, so the path is reachable. Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists, and not cosmetic: the fan-out is irreversible and Opened still increments on read (markBroadcastOpened fires when the inbox marks read, not on tap), so the admin gets no signal the destination is dead. Real, fixable validation defect — add an http(s) scheme check in validate() and a matching zod refine for type==='url' server-side.

title: Web inbox ignores deepLink and never reports opens, so the admin's Opened column undercounts
detail: The admin sends a deepLink on every broadcast and the app honours it, but the web inbox renders each row as a non-interactive <div> with no onClick and no use of `deepLink` (page.tsx:118-146) — grepping web for `deepLink` returns zero hits. Worse for the stats: web marks every unread row `read: true` in a batch on unmount (page.tsx:70-78) but never calls the `markBroadcastOpened` callable — that call exists only in the Flutter app (app/lib/features/notifications/data/notifications_repository.dart:96-109). Because markBroadcastOpened is the only writer of `broadcasts.opened` (functions/src/notifications/broadcast.ts:133) and the app only reports opens for rows it is flipping from unread→read (notifications_repository.dart:82), a row already marked read by web can never be counted afterwards.
failure_scenario: A customer opens the broadcast on the website: the row is silently marked read, the deep link is never offered so they can't reach the promoted product, and `broadcasts.opened` is not incremented. They later open the app, where the notification already shows as read, so no open is reported there either. The admin's Notifications list shows Sent=1,240 / Opened=90 when far more people actually read it, and the campaign is judged a failure.
fix: Make the web rows clickable using the same type→route mapping the app uses (home/product/category/url), and have the web page call the `markBroadcastOpened` callable with the `broadcastId`s of the rows it is about to flip to read, in the same effect that batches the read update.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on all points. web/src/app/(shop)/account/notifications/page.tsx renders rows as non-interactive divs and never touches deepLink — grep for deepLink|markBroadcastOpened|broadcast across all of web/src returns zero hits, so it is genuinely dead on that surface even though the admin always sends a deepLink (NotificationCreatePage.tsx:91-98, defaulting to type:'home' but supporting product/category/url) and the CF persists it onto each inbox doc (functions/src/notifications/broadcast.ts:52). The stats half is worse and unambiguously a defect: broadcasts.opened is written only twice — initialised to 0 at broadcast.ts:46 and incremented at broadcast.ts:133 inside markBroadcastOpened — and there are NO Firestore triggers anywhere in functions/src (grep onDocumentUpdated/onDocumentWritten is empty), so nothing server-side backfills opens from the read flag. markBroadcastOpened is guarded only by requireCustomer (guards.ts:28-31, just req.auth) and web/src/lib/firebase.ts:23 exports a configured asia-south1 functions instance, so web could call it and simply does not. Meanwhile web's unmount effect (page.tsx:70-78) batch-sets read:true on every unread row, and the app only attributes opens for rows it flips from unread (markAllRead queries where read==false; markRead guards on wasUnread), making the loss permanent. The admin surfaces the undercount directly at NotificationsListPage.tsx:101 (num(b.opened)). Not on the exclusion lists: the ALREADY-FIXED note 'broadcasts.opened counted' landed only in the Flutter app plus the callable; web was never wired and actively poisons later counting. Extra detail for the fixer: packages/shared/src/types/customers.ts:197 types deepLink as a string and omits broadcastId entirely, while the CF writes an object {type,target,label}, so a web fix must read raw doc fields or the shared type must be corrected first.

title: "Send similar" row action prefills nothing — it just opens a blank create form
detail: The only item in the per-row DropdownMenu is `{ label: 'Send similar', onClick: () => navigate('/notifications/create') }` (NotificationsListPage.tsx:111-119). It passes no router state, no query string and no id, and NotificationCreatePage initialises every field to empty/default (`useState('')`, audience 'all', linkType 'home' — NotificationCreatePage.tsx:37-41) with no location.state or param reading anywhere in the file. So the action is indistinguishable from the header's "+ Create notification" button.
failure_scenario: Admin finds last month's best-performing broadcast in the list, opens the row menu and clicks "Send similar" expecting the title, message, audience and deep link to be copied in for a quick tweak. They land on a completely blank form and must retype everything — and since the list never displays the old body or deep link, they cannot even copy it from the previous row.
fix: Pass the source broadcast through router state (`navigate('/notifications/create', { state: { from: b } })`) and seed the create page's useState initialisers from `useLocation().state?.from` (title, body, audience, deepLink.type/target).

verdict.reason: Confirmed as written. NotificationsListPage.tsx:111-119 contains a single row-menu item labelled 'Send similar' whose onClick is `navigate('/notifications/create')` — no state, no query string, no id — identical to the header's '+ Create notification' (line 47) and the dashboard QuickAction. NotificationCreatePage.tsx:37-41 initialises every field blank (title/body '', audience 'all', linkType 'home', target '') and the file contains no useLocation/useParams/useSearchParams/store read, so nothing can hydrate it; router.tsx:100 registers only the parameterless '/notifications/create' route. Attempts to refute failed: the control is reachable (DropdownMenu portals and fires onClick normally) and the flow is live (adminSendBroadcastNotification is exported at functions/src/index.ts:55 / notifications/broadcast.ts:33); no other surface (web/, app/, functions/, packages/shared) implements a duplicate/template mechanism; and the item is not cosmetic because the list shows no body or deepLink column, so the promised values are unrecoverable from the UI. It is trivially fixable since the Broadcast row already carries title, body, audience, audienceLabel and deepLink (api/notifications.ts:19-36). Not on the already-fixed or known-intentional lists.
